- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.20) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% buffer to avoid premature bottoming.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is trending up, model often overfits momentum; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overcorrection.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price drops >3% from prior high), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 prior-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before projecting.
